focus: traceability — the speckit YAML packet_goal blocks as executable instructions, and the Devin adapter chain

findingDetails.title: Speckit YAML sanctions a direct table-row append, the one write path the core serializes and guards
findingDetails.evidence: The same instruction ships in three command contracts (speckit-plan.yaml:195, speckit-implement.yaml:160, speckit-complete.yaml:253): progress goes to the goal log 'through the goal command's log action or a direct table-row append'. The log action is the only path that holds the per-packet lock (goal-core.cjs:1050) and refuses a write that changes the durable slice (:1069-1073); README.md:60 states that contract. The OpenCode plugin exposes no log action (opencode-goal.js:168 GOAL_ACTIONS list; goal-opencode.md:3,34 mirrors it), so on the primary runtime the sanctioned direct append is the only available path and it bypasses both protections.
findingDetails.impact: An agent following the YAML literally writes unlocked, and a second session can lose a row (F101 reproduces the mechanism) or move the durable slice without the refusal that exists to catch exactly that.
findingDetails.recommendation: Drop the direct-append clause or scope it to runtimes with no log action and to edits below the log anchor. Report only; no fix in this review.
findingDetails.scopeProof: Three YAML copies, the lock and guard lines, the plugin action list and the command router read directly.

findingDetails.title: Two Devin UserPromptSubmit hooks write the same additionalContext field and the host merge rule is unrecorded
findingDetails.evidence: .devin/hooks.v1.json registers spec-gate-classify.mjs (:50) and goal-inject.mjs (:55) in one UserPromptSubmit chain (goal-inject also on SessionStart, :33). spec-gate-classify.mjs:19-21 emits hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext = question; goal-inject.mjs:70-74 emits hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext = brief + reminder for the same event. Each hook is tested alone (spec-gate-devin.test.mjs), no test runs both, and the packet's own Known Limitations record host injection caps outside OpenCode as unknown.
findingDetails.impact: If Devin keeps one output per event the goal brief or the spec-gate question is dropped silently on a runtime the packet claims as a supported goal surface; the repository cannot settle which one wins.
findingDetails.recommendation: Confirm the merge rule with a two-hook smoke test and record it in the runtime matrix, or move the goal injection to an event the spec gate does not share. Report only; no fix in this review.
findingDetails.scopeProof: Both hook commands, both emitters and the goal adapter's header comment read directly; no combined test exists in the repository.
